newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges slip.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel oil barges slip.

text.p: High sulphur cracked fuel oil barges were softer on Monday as Christmas lethargy suffused the markets, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded in the morning at $116 fob ARA but prices then slipped as an ARA refiner sold barges. Afternoon trades were heard concluded at $114.
"It is fairly slow," a trader said.
High sulphur cargoes were notionally little changed, with support still seen from Romanian buying.
An Italian refiner sold a small Jan-loading three percent sulphur cargo to another player, who paid a p+c floating price.
Low sulphur prices were weaker and traders said poor demand from Italy was a key factor behind the product's weakness.
January low sulphur swaps were last heard traded at $125.50 a tonne, and traders said physical numbers were likely to be slightly above this level.

But one trader at an oil major said he was offering a small early-January cargo out of Scandinavia, and it would be available for $125 or lower. He said he had seen buying interest from a trader who already held a cargo of low sulphur fuel oil.
